# Setup

We're using a new package called `reticulate` to run Python code from within R.

```{r packages, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(reticulate)
```

```{python}
# https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bailey%E2%80%93Borwein%E2%80%93Plouffe_formula
import math
sum(16 ** -k * (4/(8*k+1) - 2/(8*k+4) - 1/(8*k+5) - 1/(8*k+6)) for k in range(100)) - math.pi
```

# Read Data

```{r read-data, message=FALSE}
daily_rides <- read_csv("data/day.csv")
```

```{r}
daily_rides_long <- 
  daily_rides %>% 
  pivot_longer(c(casual, registered, total),
               names_to = "type", values_to = "rides") %>% 
  filter(type != "total")
daily_rides_long
```


```{python}
rides = r.daily_rides_long
rides.info()
```

```{python}
rides['date'].iloc[0]
```


```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
sns.relplot(x = "date", y = "rides", hue="workingday", col="type", kind = "line", data = rides)
plt.show()
```

```{r fig.width=10}
(ggplot(daily_rides, aes(x = date, y = registered, color = workingday)) +
  geom_line() +
  theme_minimal()) %>% 
  plotly::ggplotly()
```

```{r}
daily_rides %>% 
  plotly::plot_ly(x = ~date, y = ~registered, color = ~workingday) %>% 
  plotly::add_lines()
```
